reasons: Numerator uses sum(rate(hits)) while Datadog formula uses avg for query1; the denominator also uses avg(rate(hits)), so the two terms of the formula are aggregated inconsistently and differently from the source.
The Datadog host template variable ($host with prefix host, default *) should become host=~"$host" on both queries, but the candidate drops the host matcher entirely, so the series set is wrong.

Datadog queries are raw avg values without rate(); the candidate applies rate() to the counters. The ratio of rates over the same window is a reasonable approximation, but it is not the same quantity as the raw-value ratio and should be stated.
The $scope variable (no prefix, default *) is correctly dropped and $key is unused in the queries, so those are fine.

Outcome is translated and the formula's *100 constant comes from the Datadog source, so no blocking rule is violated; the metrics are monotonic sums and rate() is allowed. The fix is to use avg aggregation consistently for both terms and add the host=~"$host" matcher on both selectors.
